candidate_claims.claim_text: Across the 18 rows of analytics/candidate_telemetry.jsonl with run_date 2026-11-24 at repository pin 9571a9a6c6bc4e6f02408b222d9be78e00818d6d, the set of rows with a non-zero $.verdict_v2.rings.ip_as_investment.lexical_subtotal (3 rows: 13, 12, 9) and the set of rows whose $.verdict_v2.nexus is 'established' or 'asserted' (4 rows: three pca_press notices at 'established' and one iareporter_headlines tribunal-constitution notice at 'asserted') are disjoint, with an intersection of 0; the single row whose ip_as_investment strength is 'present' on a body the instrument read carries nexus 'absent'.
candidate_claims.supporting_locator: analytics/candidate_telemetry.jsonl, rows with run_date == '2026-11-24', fields $.verdict_v2.nexus and $.verdict_v2.rings.ip_as_investment.lexical_subtotal; rows matched to locators in state/seen.json by sha256_hex(url) per src/telemetry.py:183; run in session with python3 -I. LIMITS, binding: (1) this is ONE run of 18 rows and is NOT a claim about the all-time 488-row telemetry corpus, which was not measured; (2) it is NOT a defect claim -- every value is correct by the field's own definitions at prompts/classifier_v2.txt:162-174, where 'established' requires an identified proceeding and 'absent' may be returned only from a read body; (3) the strong-nexus side has n=4, three of them one source on one day, and no probability model is offered because the 18 are not a random draw; (4) the access-regime explanation (that no row in the run both identifies a proceeding and exposes a readable body) is an explanation of these 18 rows and would be falsified by any corpus row that does both, which was not screened for.

Republic of Turkiye (ICSID Case No. ARB/26/40)'. By contrast https://icsid.worldbank.org/cases/pending returns ok at about 74 KB while 'ARB/' and 'ICSID Case No.' both return find_matched false on two separate dates.
